newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower ahead of CME data.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end lower ahead of CME data.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mostly lower, weighed down by expectations of increased hog marketings later this week while pork bellies ended down in light trade ahead of the CME Out-of-Town report, traders said.
Expectations that hog marketings will increase once the weather turns warmer kept hog futures pressured, traders said.
Lean hog futures closed 0.900 cent per lb lower to 0.050 higher with February off most at 76.275 cents.
Cash hog markets may show further strength Wednesday but hogs backed up by recent snow and cold should come to market later in the week, they said.

Commercial selling pressured nearby months while trade was mixed in deferreds. Rand Financials notably sold February through June contracts while Refco, Lind-Waldock and R.J. O'Brien bought April, pit sources said.
Hog futures finished technically weak and could fall sharply Wednesday if prices slip below 76.000 cents in nearby months, chartists said.
In hog options, LIT division of First Options bought February 77 calls and sold 79 calls early. Volatility continued to decline in February while holding firm in April and beyond, pit sources said.

Pork belly futures held in a narrow range late awaiting the weekly CME Out-Of-Town report after rallying early on local and fund buying and then falling on commercial resistance. Concern that storings may have been active last week despite recent weathered-shortened slaughter, prompted selling. But locals looked for a push to a net out movement which sparked underlying support, traders said.
After the close, the CME reported a net out-movement of 194,000 lbs compared with the bulk of early estimates of unchanged to in 600,000 lbs. This should buoy futures Wednesday, sources said.
However, action in hog futures Wednesday may influence belly futures direction instead, they added.

"If they (traders) hit the hogs 50 points (0.500 cent) through stops on the opening you are not going to find a lot of buying strength in the bellies," said Dale Benson, vice president and senior livestock analyst for Dean Witter.
Pork bellies closed 0.650 to 0.150 cent a lb lower with February off 0.375 at 80.175 cents.
